extracted.intended_audience: licensed firearms/defense articles importers, defense industry stakeholders, regulatory counsel, and public commenters on ATF rulemaking
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on ATF temporary-to-permanent import NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit public comments (and, if desired, hearing requests) on ATF's proposed rule to allow conversion of temporarily imported defense articles to permanent imports, and, separately, comply with the proposed procedural requirements for conversion applications if seeking to convert items. Includes procedural, evidentiary, and marking requirements for importers and specific topics on which ATF requests input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline and submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted in writing on or before (or, if mailed, postmarked on or before) August 6, 2026. The federal e-rulemaking portal will not accept comments after midnight Eastern Time on the last day of the comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit via Regulations.gov following its instructions or by mail to ATF Rulemaking Comments; include RIN 1140-AA68. Keep the comment tracking number if submitting online; uploads may not be immediately viewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment identification and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must include the agency name and number RIN 1140-AA68 for this notice of proposed rulemaking. Written comments submitted by mail must appear in minimum 12-point font, include the commenter's first and last name and full mailing address, and may be of any length. If handwritten, comments must be legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting through the federal e-rulemaking portal, carefully follow the website's submission instructions. ATF may post properly completed comments without change to Regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: PII and business-proprietary information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: ATF may post comments online; this includes any personally identifying information (PII) or business proprietary information (PROPIN) submitted in the body of the comment or as part of attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters who do not want PII posted should omit it from the comment body and attachments they want posted. If submitting PII as an attachment, place it in a separate attachment and mark it at the top with “CUI//PRVCY.” For PROPIN use the marking “CUI//PROPIN.” Mail submissions should likewise omit PII/PROPIN from the body and place such information on the cover sheet marked “CUI//PRVCY” or “CUI//PROPIN.” See the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION confidentiality section for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for public hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person who desires an opportunity to comment orally at a public hearing should submit his or her request in writing to the Director within the 90-day comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director reserves the right to determine, in light of all circumstances, whether a public hearing is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics and questions ATF specifically seeks comment on
rubrics_metrics.description: ATF requests comments on the clarity of the proposed rule and how it may be made easier to understand; on the costs or benefits of the proposed rule; and on the appropriate methodology and data for calculating those costs and benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATF seeks information on: (1) What paperwork or other burdens would be reduced by not needing to export firearms or destructive devices prior to re-importing as a permanent import, or destroying them? Would those burden savings be partially offset by different paperwork or other burdens for converting from temporary to permanent status? (2) What savings or other benefits would importers and others in the industry accrue from no longer having to export and re-import, or destroy, temporary imports? Also provide data/methodology for quantifying costs/benefits and information relevant to PRA/OIRA review (frequency of conversion filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act / information-collection comment request
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would impact OMB control number 1140-0005 (ATF Form 5330.3A, Form 6, part I) and likely increase the number of respondents completing that form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATF requests comments regarding the potential frequency with which an importer might apply to convert a temporary import to permanent using the proposed process and any PRA-related burdens or changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criteria for conversion applications (27 CFR 447.42(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will approve such applications if: (i) The licensed importer submits the information as required by paragraph (c)(1); (ii) The items being converted may be imported consistent with the provisions of this part, the Gun Control Act (18 U.S.C. chapter 44), and the National Firearms Act (26 U.S.C. chapter 53); (iii) Permanently importing the items would not violate any other federal law or regulation; and (iv) At the time the application was submitted, the firearms were lawfully present in the United States pursuant to a valid temporary import license (DSP-61) issued by the Department of State (or an exemption under 22 CFR 123.4) or in compliance with entry clearance requirements under 15 CFR 758.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four conjunctive conditions are the statutory/regulatory standards ATF will apply when deciding conversion applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content and evidentiary requirements for conversion (27 CFR 447.42(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a licensed importer wishes to permanently import items already in the United States pursuant to a temporary import license (DSP-61) or pursuant to DOC entry clearance requirements (15 CFR 758.10), the importer must submit a Form 6, part I and attach a copy of the DSP-61, entry documents showing claimed ITAR exemption, or a copy of the temporary import entry clearance documents provided to CBP pursuant to 15 CFR 758.10. Importers must also indicate on Form 6, part I that they intend to convert the temporary import to a permanent import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importers must complete Form 6 as if the item were being imported directly from the foreign source from which it was temporarily imported and include the attachments/evidence described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 6 (ATF Form 5330.3A) content and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons required to obtain a permit must file Form 5330.3A, Application/Permit to Import Firearms, Ammunition, and Defense Articles (“Form 6, part I”). The application must be signed and dated and must contain the information requested on the form, including: importer's name, address, telephone number, license and registration number (if any); country from which importing; foreign seller and foreign shipper's name and address; description of the defense article (manufacturer, type, caliber/gauge/size, model, barrel length, overall length, serial number if known, whether new or used, quantity, unit cost, category of USMIL); specific purpose for importing, including final recipient if different; and certification of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For licensed importers importing firearms, the Form 6 must be submitted in triplicate (see §478.112(b)(1)). If approved the Form 6 serves as the permit for the specified period; if disapproved ATF will notify the reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 6A (Release/Receipt) preparation and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The importer must prepare ATF Form 5330.3C, Release/Receipt of Imported Firearms, Ammunition, and Defense Articles (“Form 6A”), in duplicate, and furnish the original Form 6A to the CBP officer releasing the firearm, firearm barrel, or ammunition. Form 6A must contain requested information including importer's name/address/license number; manufacturer's name; country of manufacture; type; model; caliber/gauge/size; serial number (if known); and number of items released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will, after certification, send Form 6A to the address specified on the form. For converted items, importers must submit a Form 6A to ATF (not CBP) within the 15-day marking/filing window described in §478.112(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking requirements and timing for converted firearms (§478.112(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For firearms imported under a Department of State authorization or Department of Commerce entry clearance requirements that were not marked in accordance with paragraph (d) (e.g., pursuant to a marking exception) and were later converted to a permanent import pursuant to 27 CFR 447.42(c), importers must add identifying markings as prescribed in §478.92 or §479.102 within 15 days after ATF approves the conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importers must also submit a Form 6A to ATF within that same 15-day period identifying the converted items, including serial numbers, and noting they are converted items. Importers do not need to submit a copy of Form 6A to CBP for converted items because those items were released from CBP custody when temporarily imported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for denial under AECA and other statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under existing regulation at 27 CFR 447.44, ATF has the authority to deny applications for AECA import permits (which would include conversion applications) when importing as requested would be “inconsistent with the purpose or in violation of” the AECA or its implementing regulations in 27 CFR part 447. Additionally, ATF would deny applications if the conversion does not comply with the import provisions of the GCA and NFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure conversions are fully consistent with AECA, GCA, NFA, and other applicable federal laws/regulations to avoid denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration, revocation, and status of approved conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications approved under 27 CFR 447.42(c), the Director will indicate they are valid unless and until revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval is not perpetual if subsequently revoked; keep records and maintain compliance with ongoing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and other regulatory obligations post-conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 15 days after CBP releases (or, for converted items, after ATF approves conversion), the licensed importer must submit required forms, place required identification data on each imported firearm that lacked such data, and post all required information about the import in the records the importer is required to maintain under subpart H. ATF approval of conversion does not relieve importers or owners from statutory or regulatory provisions, including record-keeping or notice obligations, administered or enforced by the agency that approved the items' temporary import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importers must continue to comply with subpart H recordkeeping, NFA/GCA reporting, and any obligations imposed by DOS/DOC related to the item's prior temporary authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and jurisdictional rule for 'importing' vs temporary imports
rubrics_metrics.description: ATF proposes to revise §447.11 so that 'Importing (or importation)' is defined as bringing into the United States any article on the Import List, but explicitly stating that importing does not include intransit, temporary import, or temporary export transactions subject to ITAR (22 CFR parts 120–130) or EAR (15 CFR parts 730–774) while within a valid ITAR authorization or a valid EAR entry clearance. However, if an importer converts such articles to remain in the United States permanently in compliance with procedures at §447.42, they fall under this definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ITAR/EAR jurisdiction remains until DOS/DOC recognizes a change in end user or end use; conversions must comply with both ATF procedures and any continuing ITAR/EAR conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain writing and regulatory drafting objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: ATF is making plain writing and technical amendments to improve readability—using the term “importing” instead of “importation,” reducing passive voice, substituting 'U.S. Customs and Border Protection' and 'CBP' for 'Customs,' and updating headings and form numbers and names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATF explicitly requests comment on the clarity of the proposed rule and how to make it easier to understand; commenters may suggest alternative wording, organization, or plain-language edits.
